page: Microsoft Azure D4ds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Ddsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C x86_64 processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The processor includes a 480 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

This server includes 236 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable, allowing for high-performance disk configurations. It does not include any bundled public IPv4 addresses or GPU accelerators.

Benchmark data indicates highly capable single-threaded performance, with gzip compression reaching a top-tier 36.47 GB/sec and bzip3 single-threaded decompression scoring a strong 15.05 GB/sec. However, multi-core scaling shows some limitations; stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression are rated as weak. Memory read bandwidth is average at 344.82 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 43.94 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, while large block write bandwidth is weak at 23.77 GB/sec. Passmark CPU, database operations, and Redis SET operations all fall within the average tier.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the D4ds_v7 offers a balanced resource density suitable for workloads that require strong single-threaded execution and local temporary storage without the premium cost of memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated instances. It is well-suited for general-purpose workloads, including static web serving, light database operations, and single-threaded data processing tasks.
description: The Microsoft Azure D4ds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C x86_64 processor running at 4.2 GHz. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs (2 physical cores with Hyper-Threading), 16.0 GB of RAM, and 236 GB of local storage. Operating under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance supports advanced vector and matrix extensions (AVX-512 and AMX). Performance benchmarks reveal exceptional single-threaded capabilities, highlighted by top-tier gzip compression and strong bzip3 decompression. However, multi-core scaling and large-block memory write speeds are relatively weak. With average performance in database operations, Redis SET transactions, and static web serving, the D4ds_v7 represents a balanced hardware profile. It is best suited for general-purpose applications, lightweight databases, and single-threaded processing tasks requiring local temporary storage.
